2. Facts, relevant for disposal of the Rule, in brief, are that, the present opposite party, as plaintiff, had filed Title Suit No. 1313 of 1985, before the Court of the Assistant Judge, Rajbari, against the present petitioners, as defendant Nos. 1 and 2 and against the Government of Bangladesh, represented by the then Deputy Commissioner, Faridpur (now Deputy Commissioner, Rajbari), as defendant No. 3, for establishment of title and recovery of possession by evicting the defendants in respect of 20 decimals of land out of 30 decimals of land of CS Plot No. 421, RS Plot No. 396 under Mouja Shailkathi, PS and District Rajbari. The case of the plaintiff is that she had granted settlement of 20 decimals of land in her favour by a registered Patta (deed of grant) on 13th Kartic, 1340 BS and handed over possession of the suit property to her. However, the said deed was executed with reference to the CS Plot, since at that time RS operation was not done. Thereafter, the plaintiff has been possessing and enjoying the suit property through her husband and it has also been alleged that, subsequently the said property of Shomser Mollah along with his other property were sold in auction for arrear of rent, which was purchased by defendant Nos. 1 and 2 by way of auction (petitioners) and the title of Shomsher Molla has ceased and the aforesaid auction purchasers become the owners and acquired title in the suit property. The defendants thereafter increased the rent of the settled property and she was paying rent since 1362 BS and after death of her husband she is looking after the suit property. However, because of the said auction sale, the title of the suit property was not extinguished and she is continuing possession in the suit property. It has been stated that during RS operation, the said 30 decimals of land in RS Plot No. 396 was recorded in the name of the defendants-auction-purchasers, however, the plaintiff continuing possession to the eastern portion of the suit property and she was dispossessed on 11th Kartic, 1386 BS Hence, the suit. 

 13. However, having examining the deposition of PW 1 (son of the plaintiff), I find that, he deposed that he got the Patta (Exhibit 1) from a Wooden Locker of their house in 1386 BS along with two rent receipts purportedly showing payment of rent to the superior landlord. 

 15. On the other hand, on a mere comparison of the two rent receipts [Exhibit 2 and 2(Ka)] allegedly showing payment of rents on behalf of the plaintiff, I find that it was written by the same person who wrote the Patta deed. Moreover, mere perusal of these 3 documents marked as Exhibit 1, 2 and 2(Ka) clearly shows that these were manufactured by the plaintiff in connivance with the deed writer Sree Jonab Ali Sheikh and the case of the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 that the deed is fabricated and fraudulent gets support from these three documents of the plaintiff.
